author: Brian Dillon
source: “How How How What What What How—When” Suppose a Sentence (2020)

author: Edward Dahlberg
quote: Only those who know the ocean ponder death as they behold it, whereas those bound closely to the ground are more sensual.

author: Henry Miller
quote: Nothing, on deep analysis, proves to be what it seems or purports to be. Man continues to hunger.

author: Henry Miller
quote: Never was the fear of life so rampant. The fear of life has replaced the fear of death.

author: Jorge Luis Borges
quote: We could not deceive one another, and that makes conversation hard.
source: “The Other” from The Book of Sand (1975)

author: Kenneth Koch
quote: Isn’t this history, and aren’t we a couple of ruins
source: “In Love with You” (First published in Apr. 1955, Poetry Magazine )

author: Marianne Moore
quote: Dürer would have seen a reason for living in a town like this, with eight stranded whales to look at; with the sweet sea air coming into your house

author: Natsume Sōseki
quote: However you look at it, the human world is not an easy place to live.

author: Natsume Sōseki
quote: The early Zen priest Daie is said to have suffered greatly from the fact that even the enlightened mind, which has mastered the illusion of reality, is still troubled by dreams of the vulgar world.

author: Natsume Sōseki
quote: The main path has become indistinguishable among the numerous tracks that meet and part and intersect. All are a path of some sort, and none is the path itself.

author: Roland Barthes
quote: Better the illusions of subjectivity than the impostures of objectivity. Better the Imaginary of the subject than its censorship.
source: The Preparation of the Novel (Session of December 2, 1978)

author: Roland Barthes
quote: ...despite the fact that they keep happening, these ‘catastrophes’ are never planned for: the weather only exists after the event, as a discourse of irresponsibility.
source: The Preparation of the Novel (Session of January 20, 1979)

author: Susan Sontag
quote: I took a trip to see the beautiful things.
note: By way of Brian Dillon’s “Suppose a Sentence”

author: Oscar Milosz
quote: You, sad, sad sound of rain on the rain

author: Witold Gombrowicz
quote: He intended nothing at all because he wrote the way a child pees against a tree, in order to relieve himself.

author: Honoré de Balzac
quote: How many horrible and beautiful things!
section: Selected Epigraphs — "The Collected Notebooks Vols. 4–7: The Words of Others"

author: Fernando Pessoa
quote: Living life falsely and in dreams is still living life.
section: Selected Epigraphs — "The Collected Notebooks Vols. 4–7: The Words of Others"
